clue.text: Classic sort of horse, a hard worker

definitions.meaning: the wooden horse the Greeks used to get inside Troy, from classical legend
someone who works like a ... works tirelessly

explanation.surface: A description of a classic breed of horse that is a hard worker, like a carthorse.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greeks' hollow siege horse at Troy carries this name, and the idiom 'work like a Trojan' makes it a tireless labourer.

clue.text: Appropriate dinner, maybe

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to appropriate is to seize or remove something for oneself
a meal bought from a shop to eat at home, of which dinner is one example

explanation.definitionFit: To appropriate is to seize and remove for yourself; a meal bought ready-cooked from a restaurant is the noun sense.

clue.text: Fly in it? That would be a problem

definitions.text: Fly in it? That would be a problem

parts.words: Fly in it? That would be a problem
parts.note: plays on the idiom about a fly in a salve, meaning a small flaw that spoils everything

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'a fly in the ointment' means a small snag spoiling an otherwise good situation, so the salve itself is what the fly lands in.

clue.text: World's first home brew ?

parts.note: the world's first man in Genesis had only plain water to drink, the jocular name for which credits him with the brew

explanation.definitionFit: A jocular old name for drinking water, as the only drink available to the first man in the Bible.

clue.text: Conference provider offers three school subjects, plus English

parts.note: PE is physical education, a school subject
art is a school subject
RE is religious education, a school subject

explanation.surface: A conference organiser lists three school subjects plus English on its programme.
explanation.walkthrough: Conference is a variety of pear, so the tree that bears it provides the Conference; the surface wants a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Conference is a well-known British variety of pear, so the fruit tree it grows on provides it.

clue.text: Current on Nile is liable to fluctuate

indicators.note: something liable to fluctuate keeps changing, so the letters of the clue words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that the current on the river Nile is prone to rise and fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liable to fluctuate' rearranges ONNILE into the Pacific current; 'is' joins definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A periodic warm ocean current in the Pacific that disrupts weather worldwide.

clue.text: Damp and unhealthy, but spacious, it's said

indicators.note: signals that the word for spacious is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a spacious room is roomy

explanation.surface: Describing a house that is damp and unhealthy but has plenty of space.
explanation.definitionFit: Watery, catarrhal eyes or a damp, raw climate are described with this word, linked to rheum, a watery discharge.

clue.text: Those who succeed must hope for long ones

definitions.text: Those who succeed must hope for long ones

parts.words: Those who succeed must hope for long ones
parts.note: those who succeed to the throne hope for lengthy periods of rule

explanation.definitionFit: Monarchs who succeed to a throne hope their periods of rule will be long.

clue.text: Moral code devised by the sick, mostly

indicators.note: something devised is put together anew, so the letters are rearranged
most of the words, so the final letter of the sick is dropped

explanation.surface: A moral code drawn up by people who are ill, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of THE SICK to leave THESIC, and 'devised' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of moral principles governing behaviour is a synonym for a moral code.

clue.text: Livingstone converted any African

parts.note: Ken Livingstone, a former Mayor of London

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The explorer Livingstone brings an African to Christianity.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests David Livingstone, the missionary explorer; it is Ken Livingstone, London's former mayor. 'converted' rearranges ANY into YAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from a country in East Africa, so a kind of African.

clue.text: Stoned after a joint that's very small

indicators.note: the word for stoned comes after the joint

parts.note: the knee is a joint of the leg
stoned means intoxicated by drugs, high

explanation.surface: Someone stoned after smoking a joint feels tiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests a cannabis cigarette beside 'Stoned', but it is a body joint.
explanation.definitionFit: Only as tall as a person's leg joint, an idiom for being a small child.

clue.text: A majority welcome the Left, just about

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
most means the majority

explanation.surface: Most voters, nearly all of them, welcome a party of the Left.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearly or very nearly, a synonym of just about.

clue.text: Careless men with woman who needs a reminder

indicators.note: careless suggests sloppily arranged, so the letters are rearranged
the woman needs, is lacking, the letter a

parts.note: Monica is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Careless men living with a woman who needs to remind them of everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Careless' rearranges MEN into MNE; 'who needs a' says MONICA lacks an A, leaving MONIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A memory aid such as a rhyme or acronym, which serves as a reminder.

clue.text: Among flying insects the queen produces young

indicators.note: the queen is placed among the letters of the insects

parts.note: moths are flying insects
ER is the abbreviation for Elizabeth Regina, the queen

explanation.surface: In a colony of flying insects, the queen alone lays eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints a queen insect; the queen is ER.
explanation.definitionFit: To mother is to give birth to or raise offspring, so produces young.

clue.text: Low part of upland area

indicators.note: only part of the word for upland area is used, the last letter dropped

parts.note: a moor is an open upland area

explanation.surface: A remark about the low-lying part of a hilly region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' reads as low-lying, but it is the noise a cow makes.
explanation.definitionFit: To low is to make the sound a cow makes, a synonym.

clue.text: Historical records of plants university lost

indicators.note: the university letter is lost from the plants word

parts.note: annuals are plants that live for one year

explanation.surface: Historical records of plants that a university has mislaid.
explanation.definitionFit: Year-by-year chronicles of events, so historical records.

clue.text: Advance with vehicle in reverse!

indicators.note: the vehicle is read backwards

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle

explanation.surface: An instruction to move forward with a vehicle that is reversing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advance' is the noun: a loan against wages.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal word for a loan against future pay, a sense of advance.

clue.text: Where to stay in financial centre

indicators.note: the centre letter of the word financial is taken

explanation.surface: A suggestion of a hotel in the heart of the financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub or small hotel offering lodging, a place to stay.

clue.text: European fraud that sounds wonderful

parts.note: EU is the abbreviation for European, as in the European Union
a phony is a fraud or fake

explanation.surface: A European con artist whose pitch sounds terrific.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasing, harmonious sound; the definition means something that sounds wonderful.

clue.text: Time to reserve one of 14

parts.note: a year is a period of time
to book is to reserve

explanation.surface: Time to reserve a place for one of the entries at 14.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 is the answer at 14 across, historical records; a volume recording a year's events is one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: An annual publication recording a year's events, an example of the historical records at 14 across.

clue.text: Speeds up — cause of accident on the stairs?

definitions.meaning: to step out is to walk faster

definitions.text: cause of accident on the stairs?
definitions.meaning: a step being out of place on a staircase could make someone fall

explanation.definitionFit: To quicken one's pace when walking is one sense; a missing tread on a staircase would cause a fall.

clue.text: It blows up reckless general, starting rout

indicators.note: reckless suggests wild, so the letters are rearranged
the starting letter of the word rout is taken

explanation.surface: A reckless general blows things up, setting off a rout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reckless' rearranges GENERAL into ENLARGE; 'starting' takes R, the first letter of rout.
explanation.definitionFit: A photographic device that makes a larger print, blowing up an image.

clue.text: Scientist using kind of light tube with weight inserted

indicators.note: the weight abbreviation is put inside the tube word

parts.note: a neon tube is a kind of light

explanation.surface: A scientist experimenting with a fluorescent tube that has a weight inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Newton was the English physicist and mathematician.

clue.text: Failed to bid spades, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly hints at an unexpected order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bridge player unexpectedly fails to bid in spades.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, declining to bid on one's turn is to pass, so having done so.

clue.text: What man on the run fears yet wants, reportedly

definitions.text: What man on the run fears

indicators.note: signals that the words are spoken aloud, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: what a fugitive wants is a breather, a rest

explanation.surface: A fugitive both dreads and longs for the same thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What man on the run' does double duty: he fears capture yet wants 'a rest', which sounds the same; 'yet' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being taken into custody by police is what a fugitive dreads.

clue.text: Bandleader once worked with Rolling Stones

definitions.meaning: Glenn ..., the American swing bandleader of the 1940s
a grinder of corn works with millstones that roll

explanation.definitionFit: Glenn Miller led a famous swing band; a person who grinds grain works with turning millstones.

clue.text: Peer spotted in party, oddly

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of party are taken

explanation.surface: A nobleman seen at a party behaving strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' looks like a lord; it is the verb, to look closely or snoop.
explanation.definitionFit: To peer or look inquisitively, a synonym.

clue.text: Bird fancier much impressed by tail feathers

definitions.text: Bird fancier much impressed by tail feathers

parts.words: Bird fancier much impressed by tail feathers
parts.note: a female bird who fancies a male bird for his splendid fanned tail display

explanation.definitionFit: The female peafowl is courted by the male's showy tail display.

clue.text: Flying distance made by Israeli male

indicators.note: the letters are made into a new word, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An Israeli man clocks up a long flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made by' rearranges ISRAELI plus M, for male.
explanation.definitionFit: Loyalty points earned per distance flown, so a measure of flying distance.

clue.text: Granddad accepts blame — that's the spirit!

indicators.note: the granddad word accepts, takes in, the blame word

parts.note: GPA is a short form of grandpa, granddad
to take the rap is to take the blame

explanation.surface: Grandpa owns up to the blame, and everyone cheers his attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's the spirit!' is an encouraging cry; the definition is spirit, the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian brandy distilled from grape residue, a type of spirit.

clue.text: Secret way to get fit for Eastenders

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: Cockney East Londoners drop their H sounds, so the H is lost from the fit word

parts.note: fit means healthy

explanation.surface: A secret method for East Londoners to get in shape.
explanation.walkthrough: Londoners from the East End, Cockneys, famously drop the H at the start of words; EastEnders is also a British soap set there.
explanation.definitionFit: Done furtively so as not to be noticed, a synonym of secret.

clue.text: Tea provided by the pool on groundsheets

indicators.note: the letters are supplied by a run inside the words pool on groundsheets

explanation.surface: Tea served at a campsite beside the pool, laid out on groundsheets.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chinese variety of partly fermented tea.

clue.text: Change the end or do what Cromwell did

indicators.note: change means alter, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to rewrite the ending, or else act like Cromwell.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver Cromwell led the side that deposed King Charles I in the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: Cromwell's forces removed Charles I from the throne, deposing a monarch.

clue.text: Pond insect takes off by the end of summer

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged
the last letter of the word summer is taken

explanation.surface: A pond insect takes off at the close of summer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes off' reads as an insect flying away; 'off' is the anagram signal on takes, and 'by' is a link meaning next to.
explanation.definitionFit: A pond skater is a water insect that glides across the surface.
